summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled shell, arbitrary file access, and server-driven auto-upgrade to hardcoded pull.7ii.win:7999
details: On startup the package opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes the installer's host to full remote control by whoever runs that server. On TERM_OPEN messages it spawns bash or cmd.exe via node-pty and pipes TERM_INPUT bytes into the PTY, giving the remote party an interactive shell. handleScriptList / handlePolicyScripts pass server-supplied script bodies to child_process.exec and return stdout, stderr, and exit code back over the same channel. handleFileRequest implements list/read/write/delete/rename/mkdir/stat against any absolute path the server names, streaming file contents back as base64 — so the operator can read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, wallet files, or source, and can modify or delete files on the host. On MsgType.UPGRADE the client runs `npm update -g newtun` and respawns itself, giving the server a push-update channel for future versions. Alongside this, the client sends host identifiers (hostname, OS type/release, arch, Node version) at auth and streams CPU, memory, uptime, load, and per-interface network rates every 5 seconds to the same server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
